title: Frayed RoPE and Long Inputs: A Geometric Perspective
claim: Separated, tightly clustered key and query clouds let a low-norm sink absorb attention; longer inputs disperse and overlap them, so the sink fails.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, matching 2D axes with Keys/Queries regions and sink dot
description: Two side-by-side 2D coordinate diagrams with bold black axes. On the left, a blue quarter-annulus labeled Keys sits in the upper right and a peach quarter-annulus labeled Queries sits in the lower left. The two clouds are cleanly separated and each is a tight band. A blue dot k lies on the vertical axis and an orange dot q lies on the horizontal axis. A small black dot near the origin is labeled sink. On the right, the keys and queries are drawn as two large, mostly overlapping circles in blue and peach. The overlap is a muddy gray-brown. The k and q dots now sit close together inside the overlap, and the sink dot is inside the cloud. The eye goes first to the colored shapes, then to the contrast between separation on the left and overlap on the right.
caption: A 2D diagram of our observed latent geometry. Left: Keys/queries cluster tightly into opposing point clouds with negative dot products. The sink token has low norm and thus the greatest dot product. Matched key/query pair $q,k$ align orthogonally, letting their product approach and exceed the sink's. Right: RoPE on long inputs makes keys/queries disperse and overlap, causing spurious alignment. Sink token stops functioning.
abstract: Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE) is a widely adopted technique for encoding position in language models, which, while effective, causes performance breakdown when input length exceeds training length. Prior analyses assert (rightly) that long inputs cause channels to rotate ``out of distribution,'' but it is not clear how extra rotation relates to or causes pathological behavior. Through empirical and theoretical analysis we advance a unified geometric understanding of attention behavior with RoPE. We find that attention induces tight clustering of separated key and query latent point clouds, allowing for creation of sink tokens: placeholders that allow attention heads to avoid token mixing when not required. RoPE applied to longer inputs damages this key/query cluster separation, producing pathological behavior by inhibiting sink token functionality. From this geometric perspective, we propose RoPE-ID (In Distribution), a straightforward modification that allows attention layers to generalize to longer inputs out of the box: apply RoPE with high frequency to a subset of channels. We demonstrate the effectiveness of RoPE-ID for extended inputs using 1B and 3B parameter Transformers on the LongBench and RULER information retrieval benchmarks.
